imo-1974-01.prompt:
Three players $A$, $B$ and $C$ play the following game: On each of three cards an integer is written. These three numbers $p, q, r$ satisfy $0 < p < q < r$. The three cards are shuffled and one is dealt to each player. Each then receives the number of counters indicated by the card he holds. Then the cards are shuffled again; the counters remain with the players.

This process (shuffling, dealing, giving out counters) takes place for at least two rounds. After the last round, $A$ has $20$ counters in all, $B$ has $10$ and $C$ has $9$. At the last round $B$ received $r$ counters. Who received $q$ counters on the first round?

imo-1974-02.prompt:
In the triangle $ABC$, prove that there is a point $D$ on side $AB$ such that $CD$ is the geometric mean of $AD$ and $DB$ if and only if
$$\sin A\,\sin B \le \sin^2\frac{C}{2}.$$
imo-1974-02.answer: Proof: by the power of a point, $CD^2=AD\cdot DB$ iff $D$ is the midpoint of the chord $CE$ through $D$; so such $D$ exists iff some point of arc $AB$ (not containing $C$) is at distance $h_c$ from $AB$, i.e. iff $h_c=2R\sin A\sin B\le 2R\sin^2\frac C2$ (the height of that arc).

imo-1974-03.prompt: Prove that the number $\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{n}\binom{2n+1}{2k+1}2^{3k}$ is not divisible by $5$ for any integer $n\ge 0$.
imo-1974-03.answer: Proof: write $(1+\sqrt8)^{2n+1}=a+b\sqrt8$; then $b$ is the given sum and $a^2-8b^2=-7^{2n+1}$; if $5\mid b$ then $a^2\equiv\pm2\pmod 5$, impossible.

imo-1974-04.prompt:
Consider decompositions of an $8\times 8$ chessboard into $p$ non-overlapping rectangles subject to the following conditions:

(i) Each rectangle has as many white squares as black squares.

(ii) If $a_i$ is the number of white squares in the $i$-th rectangle, then $a_1<a_2<\cdots<a_p$.

Find the maximum value of $p$ for which such a decomposition is possible. For this value of $p$, determine all possible sequences $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_p$.

imo-1974-05.prompt:
Determine all possible values of
$$S=\frac{a}{a+b+d}+\frac{b}{a+b+c}+\frac{c}{b+c+d}+\frac{d}{a+c+d}$$
where $a,b,c,d$ are arbitrary positive numbers.
imo-1974-05.answer: All real numbers in the open interval $(1,2)$.

imo-1974-06.prompt:
Let $P$ be a non-constant polynomial with integer coefficients. If $n(P)$ is the number of distinct integers $k$ such that $(P(k))^2=1$, prove that
$$n(P)-\deg(P)\le 2,$$
where $\deg(P)$ denotes the degree of the polynomial $P$.
imo-1974-06.answer: Proof: if both $P=1$ and $P=-1$ have integer roots, $u-v\mid 2$ shows each equation has at most $3$ integer roots, so $n\le6\le d+2$ for $d\ge4$; small degrees are checked by hand ($d=3$: the roots of $P=1$ leave only one possible root of $P=-1$).
